[LSTR.2.2] String indexing is codepoint-indexed. `s[i]` returns
the codepoint at zero-based index `i` as a single-codepoint
`String`.

**An out-of-range index raises a `ComputationError` and abandons the
activation.** The operation is well typed — `Int` carries no length bound — so
there is no type error to raise; there is simply no answer, which is the
`ComputationError` test and the same one that places division by zero there
([LERR.1.4.10]). `len(s)` ([LSTR.2.1]) is the guard.

**A negative index is a compile error when the index is a literal**
(`s[-1]`), and a `ComputationError` when it is computed — the split
[LTIM.8.3.2] already uses for format identifiers. A literal negative
index is a bug the compiler can see.
